headline: Nvidia loses its CEO as yields and oil jump
tone: Jensen Huang is out at Nvidia after the affairs story, and the fallout is spreading to Washington, where lawmakers are pressing Howard Lutnick.
body: Jensen Huang is out at Nvidia after the affairs story, and the fallout is spreading to Washington, where lawmakers are pressing Howard Lutnick. The bigger market question is policy: tougher curbs on AI chip sales to China look more likely under new leadership. Wall Street slipped with three stocks falling for every one that rose, even as AMD, Broadcom and Arista held up the hardware trade.

Rates did the damage. Short and long Treasury yields rose sharply together, the dollar firmed against the euro, franc and yen, and gold and silver fell hard. When bonds sell off this broadly, the AI premium in equities gets harder to defend, a point the FT is pressing on the debt funding the build-out.

Oil jumped after Trump signalled an end to JD Vance's push for an Iran deal, putting the risk premium back into crude. Distillate cracks narrowed rather than following, which says this was a crude move on geopolitics, not a tighter refined market.

Gas rose hard on both sides of the Atlantic, with EU storage still below its five-year range heading into winter. In the Nordics, Friday's prices fell back across the region, with Finland again the cheapest area.

views.text: The tape was narrow: chip and networking leaders gained while the broad market fell, so investors are still paying for the AI build-out but not for much else. Europe held up better, led by insurers and Equinor as oil rallied, while Rheinmetall slipped again as Ukraine talks return to the headlines. Today's US PPI tests whether the jump in yields has further to go.

Crude priced geopolitics, not barrels: with Washington stepping back from Iran talks, the risk premium returned, while the gasoil crack gave back much of Wednesday's widening. Gas is the tighter story, with storage short of every recent year and the TTF curve holding flat through winter. Today's IEA monthly is the next read on supply.

Friday's system price fell back toward its October level, but the split across the region remains the story. Finland stays cheap on nuclear output, while southern Sweden, Denmark and southern Norway are priced off the continent. November so far has had less wind than October, and hydro has filled the gap, which draws on reservoirs heading into winter.
